newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts recover recent losses in quiet day.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts recover recent losses in quiet day.

text.p: 1520 GMT - UK gilt futures end the day up nearly 1/2 point, recovering Wednesday's losses, supported by benign U.S. inflation and industrial production data. Market quiet, helped by strength in T-bond. * Sept gilts settle up 14/32 at 114-25
Analysts said the U.S. data was important for UK markets in that Britain was closest to the United States in its economic cycle, but Thursday's data held no surprises.
"These numbers are right in line with expectations and there's nothing really new for the bond market to chew on," said Rob Hayward, economist at Bank America.
September gilt futures on LIFFE ended the day 14/32 higher at 114-25, pushing back up above Tuesday's close of 114-24, but hovering within a fairly tight range for much of the day.
Traders said it had been a quiet day overall, with no major domestic focus and only around 36,000 contracts changing hands.

"There's been a slight flattening of the curve, but we're still stuck in a range between 114 and 115," one trader said, adding that most activity occurred in sell-offs when the market touched its higher levels.
"We've have seen some selling off at these higher levels, but mostly we've been following the international markets," he said.

Analysts said the curve flattening was a logical follow-on from Wednesday's Bank of England inflation report and statement, which said any interest rate changes were on hold for the time being, but did not say for how long.

The gilts market saw an intial burst of enthusiasm when the Bank of England raised interest rates by a further quarter point last week and hinted this could be the last rise for some time, but traders began to reassess the rates outlook soon afterwards.

"The report heightened expectations that interest rates would rise agin at some stage, probably towards the end of the year and the response to that has been to flatten the curve," said Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at BZW.
Adams said talk of a German rate rise in the near future should squeeze the gilt/Bund spread in but no evidence of this had surfaced yet.
The gilt/Bund 10-year spread settled at 150 basis points, slightly wider than its early level of 149, but holding within its recent range.

At the short end of the yield curve LIFFE September short sterling settled one basis point higher at 92.77, while December was three basis points higher at 92.65, discounting a rate rise of 25 basis points by the end of the year.
